messages:
sam_sales: Heads-up: OrionEdge POC kickoff scheduled for Wed but procurement/legal surfaced blockers that must be cleared before we flip billing. TL;DR: 1) they insist on signed orderform before any invoicing, 2) DPA contains a legacy subprocessor clause that looks too permissive, 3) they say they require customer-managed HSM for keys, and 4) EU subsidiary may require wet-ink for the MSA. Looping @anya_legal @leo_procure @jin_se @maia_security @sasha_billing.

anya_legal: paste their DPA clause here pls. If it's the usual "broad transfer" language we propose notice + objection or a named-subprocessor appendix. Also propose fallback: eSign orderform for POC only with explicit carveouts so we can start.

sam_sales: Their exact snippet from counsel:
```
"Vendor may engage legacy subprocessors and transfer Customer Data internationally without prior notice, unless otherwise agreed in writing."
```

anya_legal: Yep, that's a no. Two redline options: (A) Replace with: "Vendor will maintain a subprocessor list, provide 30 days' notice of changes and Customer may object; all transfers subject to SCCs or equivalent safeguards." (B) Provide named-subprocessor appendix and require written consent for additions. I'll drop both as tracked changes.

leo_procure: On signed orderform: we can either wait for PO and activate after receipt, or accept pre-billed credits (invoice on receipt). Finance default Net30; Net45 requires commercial approval. If they insist no billing without signed orderform we need PO up front. Recommend adding a modest overage cap to the orderform (e.g., $1,500) to avoid disputes.

jin_se: Technical note: Hosted API cannot bind to customer-managed HSM. Dedicated/Private support BYO-KMS/HSM. If they require HSM for the POC, we must run Dedicated which adds provisioning lead time (~7-12 business days) and a price uplift (ballpark +20-35%). Workaround options: client-side encryption or scoped managed KMS, but procurement/security teams often don't accept those.

maia_security: Also request they complete our security questionnaire and share SOC2 report. If their EU sub claims wet-ink, ask for the regulatory/policy text that requires it. Most EU entities accept eSign with verifiable audit trails. Link: https://redwood.example.com/sec-qa.

sam_sales: I'll ask them for the EU policy excerpt. Two asks for the team now: Anya 1 drop both redline files in-thread so I can forward; Jin 1 confirm exact lead time + estimate for Dedicated+HSM; Leo/Sasha 1 confirm pre-bill vs PO and suggested overage cap.

anya_legal: Will post tracked redlines by EOD. Also adding protective language for an "eSign-first" flow: "Orderform executed electronically authorizes POC activation only; Final MSA execution (electronic or physical) governs production usage and supersedes POC terms."

jin_se: Confirmed: Dedicated provisioning ~7-12 business days for full pilot; if they accept lower throughput we can attempt a fast-track 4-5 day build with smaller instance. HSM integration must be configured during provisioning. Cost uplift estimate: +25% on POC pricing for typical pilot (range 20-35%).

sasha_billing: Billing note: Pre-bill credits OK (Net0 invoice) to unblock environment. If we accept eSign now and they later insist on wet-ink, we'll tag revenue as "POC-eSign-limited" in accounting to avoid premature recognition. Recommend $1,500 overage cap unless customer requests otherwise. Need billing contact and PO intent to proceed.

docusign-bot: Created envelope ENV-44321 for OrionEdge POC orderform (expires in 14 days). Signers: OrionEdge PO contact, sam_sales. Status: pending.

sam_sales: Proposed approach for customer: 1) eSign orderform (pre-bill credits or PO) with a $1.5k overage cap to start POC on hosted config, 2) have them complete security questionnaire and provide SOC2, 3) if they confirm HSM requirement for POC we pause hosted and provision Dedicated (new orderform, lead time/cost noted), 4) if EU sub legally requires wet-ink for MSA we can accept wet-ink for the final MSA but request eSign for POC orderform so we don't block kickoff. I'll send Anya's redlines + sec questionnaire now.

leo_procure: If they insist strictly no billing w/o signed MSA (not just orderform), we need clear escalation and PO before activation. Finance may approve Net45 for strategic pilots with one-pager justification.

anya_legal: Once customer responds to redlines we'll include fallback clause that permits eSign-limited activation with liability carveouts. That typically resolves timing friction.

maia_security: FYI: if they request Dedicated with EU-only residency + HSM, confirm desired region so we provision in the correct datacenter.

sam_sales: Good point. I'll ask about EU-only residency in the follow-up. Leaving thread open until I have the customer's reply. Thanks team :pray:
